video.title: I Built A Business From Scratch Only Following Claude's Advice

summary: Tim Richard, who owns a business in a boring industry, tests following Claude's advice to build a million-dollar business from scratch. Claude suggested niche software for boring trades, and after checking Google Ads competition Tim chose tattoo shop booking software. Claude researched competitors, produced a product plan and a build prompt, and Claude Code built Inkbook (inkbook.io) in a few days. No customers or revenue yet; part two will test paid ads. The video ends with a plug for his paid idea book.

acquisition.how: Paid search and social ads can be set up and optimised by agents with occasional human approval of budget and creative.

onboarding.how: Self-serve signup and in-app setup; templates can be automated.

delivery.how: Software runs unattended once built, apart from bug fixes.

billing.how: Subscription billing via a payments provider (e.g. Stripe) is automatic.

support.how: AI support and docs can handle most tickets; humans handle bugs and edge cases.

uk_applicability.notes: Software and ads work the same in the UK. Tattoo shops are common; local competitors and GDPR for customer data and waivers should be checked.

tactics.name: Pick a niche by checking ad competition
steps: Ask Claude for underserved niches where people search for software but competition is weak
Shortlist niches (pet grooming, pressure washing, gutter cleaning, tattoo booking)
Check which competitors exist and whether they bid on Google Ads for the keywords
Choose the niche with weak products and almost no bidders, so cost per click stays low

quote.text: Find an underserved niche where people are searching for software, but the competition is weak.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

tactics.name: AI-driven competitor feature gap build
steps: Have Claude scrape and analyse every competitor (4-5): features, pricing, positioning, strengths, weaknesses
Combine all features into one list and add differentiators
Have Claude produce a screen-by-screen product plan
Get a single build prompt and paste it into Claude Code
Iterate on bugs; ask it to explain things simply when stuck
Use Claude design for branding, logos and colours

quote.text: Claude scraped and analyzed all the major tattoo shop booking softwares out there.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

warnings.warning: Making the product does not guarantee money; the opportunities are opinions and results are not guaranteed.

quote.text: Just because you start one of these doesn't mean you're going to make money.

lessons.lesson: Choose a niche where ad competition is thin, since low cost per click is what makes paid acquisition profitable.

quote.text: If very few companies are competing for these keywords, advertising costs stay low, which means we could acquire customers profitably.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

lessons.lesson: Check whether big incumbents already cover a niche under a broader product and bid on its keywords before committing.
AI can compress product research, planning and a first build of a software product into days for a non-technical founder.
A measurable acquisition plan (paid ads) suits a founder who does not want to do outreach or become an influencer.
Building is the easy part; the real test is whether customers sign up and ads pay back, which this video has not tested yet.

quote.text: Now comes the part that actually matters. Can Claude help me get customers?
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

lessons.lesson: Domain familiarity in a boring industry helps judge whether existing software is poor.

evidence_quality.rationale: Part one of a series; it shows a built product but no customers, revenue or ad data. Claims about competitors are unverified and there are few numbers.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sells an idea book of business ideas and benefits from YouTube views for the series.
